title: Integration tests: dedicated staged rollout happy path + gate-fail path (flaky metrics + determinism)
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Adds end-to-end integration coverage for Dedicated staged rollouts, specifically: (1) happy path stage progression with deterministic traffic allocation, (2) gate failure -> auto-hold (and explicit rollback) behavior, and (3) flaky / late metric ingestion simulation to validate fail-safe behavior (pause rather than proceed) and to prevent regressions like INT-1133 (perpetual hold from missing metrics in staging).

These tests run against the control-plane + routing + evaluator stack in our integration env with fakes for metrics + time, and validate that stage allocation is stable across process restarts and evaluator ticks. This PR is intentionally heavier than unit tests because we’ve had multiple “looks fine in unit tests” issues due to timing, metric freshness, and concurrency around approval + evaluator advancement.

What’s included (high level): - New integration harness that brings up rollout service, routing policy evaluator, and gate evaluator with a controllable clock - Determinism checks for stage allocation hashing (same request key routes to same stage across restarts; no drift when stage weights unchanged) - Happy path: create plan -> Stage 1 5% -> pass gates -> manual approval -> Stage 2 25% -> pass -> Stage 3 100% - Gate fail path: intentionally degrade p95 latency + queue depth metrics for stage canary slice -> evaluator triggers hold -> routing freezes allocation -> operator abort -> traffic returns to baseline - Flaky metrics simulation: drop metric batches / delay metric timestamps beyond freshness window -> evaluator pauses with reason=MISSING_METRICS (not proceed) -> requires manual action to continue - Concurrency regression test: approval arrives concurrently with evaluator tick; asserts no double-advance (covers the race fixed in PR #28622; this test is structured to catch reintroductions)

Not included / follow-ups: - Multi-armed experimentation coverage (out of scope) - Per-request quality gates (still optional and only partially wired) - Load-focused coverage (belongs in the dedicated pool load test plan doc; we only include a small saturation sanity check here)

Implementation notes: - Uses a FakeMetricsStore with explicit “ingest_at” and “sample_time” to model late data vs missing data. We treat late/missing as fail-safe pause. - Uses a TestClock to avoid real sleeps; evaluator tick is driven by the test. - Determinism test uses a fixed set of request keys and asserts stable mapping across (a) process restart and (b) re-hydration of RolloutPlan from DB with identical plan_version.

Example assertion (trimmed):

assertMappingStable(keys, mappingBeforeRestart)
restartServices()
assertMappingStable(keys, mappingBeforeRestart)

CI: adds a new integration test shard (dedicated-rollouts-itest) that runs in ~7–9 minutes. It is marked required for merge for this directory only (does not block unrelated areas).

Risk: low for prod behavior (tests + harness only), medium for CI stability. We observed one flake due to a too-tight freshness window in the flaky-metrics case; adjusted to use a deterministic clock + explicit window boundaries.

test(integration): simulate late/missing metrics and verify fail-safe pause
test(integration): determinism checks across restart + plan rehydrate

review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Love seeing this at integration level. Two asks: (1) Please assert the plan_version is unchanged during the determinism test restart; we had a subtle issue where re-save increments version and changes evaluator behavior. (2) In the flaky metrics test, can you differentiate late vs missing in the failure reason so UI can show the right hint?

Leila Farouk (author): Good call on plan_version. Added an explicit get-plan call after restart and assert plan_version == initial. For flaky metrics, FakeMetricsStore now emits (a) missing series and (b) late timestamps; evaluator returns MISSING_METRICS vs STALE_METRICS, and tests assert both paths.

Mina Haddad (review): For the routing determinism test: can you also assert that 0% and 100% edge cases don’t produce “unassigned” routing? We saw issues during transitions.

Leila Farouk (author): Added assertions for Stage weight 0% (all keys map to baseline) and 100% (all keys map to canary) and explicitly check no key returns UNKNOWN. Also added a small randomized key set (seeded) to avoid only testing “nice” keys.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure the tests pause on missing metrics rather than auto-rollback. Ops wants hold-by-default; rollback should be explicit unless policy says otherwise.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated gate-fail test to assert auto-hold only; rollback occurs via explicit abort endpoint. Added comment referencing SRE guidance.

Thomas Baird (review): Any concern about cardinality in the fake metrics labels? I don’t want the test harness encouraging high-card patterns.

Leila Farouk (author): FakeMetricsStore defaults to low-card labels (tenant_id, pool_id, stage_id) and disallows request_id label. Added a guard that fails the test if a metric includes a label outside the allowlist.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Does the abort flow test cover RBAC? At least assert non-privileged actor gets 403.

Leila Farouk (author): Added a small RBAC negative case in the abort test: viewer token -> 403; operator token -> 200. (Full RBAC matrix coverage remains in API tests.)

Approvals: Ethan Park ✅, Mina Haddad ✅, Sean Gallagher ✅, Thomas Baird ✅, Kaitlyn Nguyen ✅
